question.leadin: Answer some questions about the early colonization of New England.
question.text: This Puritan minister founded Rhode Island after being expelled from Massachusetts. He was one of the first abolitionists and wrote the first book about Native American languages.
question.clue: Earlier in his life, he chafed at Archbishop William Laud's strict control of Anglican Church doctrine, escaping with his wife Mary to Boston.

swap.leadin: The split between "Old Lights" and "New Lights" occurred during this period.
swap.text: Evangelists like George Whitfield and Jonathan Edwards were active during what period of intense religious fervor in early colonial America?
swap.clue: A speech from this movement compares its audience to "a spider, or some loathsome insect" held over a fire.

question.leadin: This conflict was part of the larger Seven Years' War.
question.text: Name this North American war in which Britain defeated a European rival for control of Canada.
question.clue: A namesake expedition in this conflict was ambushed at the Monongahela River by forces under Daniel Beaujeu, leading to the death of General Braddock.

swap.leadin: The war saw the British under Anson attacking the Manila Galleon, after which he circumnavigated the globe.
swap.text: Identify this war that saw the battles at Porto Bello and Cartagena that was sparked by the Spanish seizure of its namesake's ship, Rebecca.
swap.clue: Seeing an unsuccessful amphibious assault on Cartagena de Indias, the incident that sparked this war involved the boarding of the ship Rebecca.

question.text: This period of famine during the history of the Jamestown colony was relieved by a supply convoy led by Baron De La Warr. Evidence of cannibalism during this period has been discovered near the Jamestown colony.
question.clue: A major cause of this period, during which some relief came from trade with the Nansemonds, was the failure of the Third Supply due to the wreck of the Sea Venture, an event which inspired The Tempest.

swap.leadin: This man began one speech by quoting the line "their foot shall slide in due time."
swap.text: Name this preacher, who compared people to spiders held above a fire in his sermon "Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God."
swap.clue: This man addressed the issue of predetermination in Freedom of the Will, written while he was in Stockbridge converting members of the Mahican and Mohawk tribes.

question.leadin: Name these founders of U.S. States.
question.text: This Quaker received permission from King James II to establish a state known for its religious tolerance, nicknamed the "Keystone State."
question.clue: In an event depicted by a Benjamin West painting, this man expanded his holdings by signing treaties with the Lenape tribe after he was given a colony by Charles II.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about rebellions in colonial America, none of which were the American Revolution.
swap.text: James II consolidated several northern colonies into this entity, led by Joseph Dudley and then Edmund Andros. Colonists revolted against Andros when word of England's Glorious Revolution spread.
swap.answer: Dominion of New England in America
swap.clue: Its first president later became chief justice of New York, and sentenced Jacob Leisler to death for treason.

question.leadin: Early in his career, this politician wrote a successful "Tragy Comedy" for Queen Henrietta Maria titled The Lost Lady.
question.text: Name this successor to Francis Wyatt who upset his white constituency by adopting friendlier relations with Native Americans. This governor died before he could explain his actions to King Charles II.
question.clue: This Virginia Governor's policies incited Bacon's Rebellion. This man was appointed by Charles I and replaced Sir Francis Wyatt.

swap.text: He replaced Willem Kieft as governor and conquered Swedish Delaware. For 15 points, identify this one-legged governor who served as the last Dutch colonial leader of New York.
swap.clue: He was also plagued by poor Indian relations, as shown by the outbreak of the Peach Tree War and conflicts near the village of Esopus, which he renamed Wildwyck.

question.leadin: Name the following from the early settling of the English in America.
question.text: This man wanted to found a colony for debtors in America and eventually got a charter from George II to start the colony of Georgia.
question.clue: This man advocated for an excise tax on malt liquor to fund a comprehensive reform of the prison system of England while head of the Gaols ] Committee.

swap.text: The Pilgrims had been attempting to reach this colony before the Mayflower was blown northward. The House of Burgesses was the elected body of the government of this colony, which was founded at Jamestown.
swap.clue: In this colony, a Doeg raid on Thomas Matthews's farm devastated the Pamunkey and deposed William Berkeley after he refused a militia appointment agreed upon by the House of Burgesses.

question.leadin: Allegedly, a settler gave a chief of this people a compass when he was about to be executed, which he saw as a peace offering.
question.text: Name these people from modern-day Virginia. John Smith claimed that these people were about to execute him until the intervention of a member of this group, Pocahontas.
question.answerHtml: Powhatan people [or Powhatan Confederacy; accept Tsenacommacah; prompt on Algonquian people]

swap.text: During the War of Jenkins' Ear, Oglethorpe led British troops against the Spanish in this battle fought in July 1742 on St. Simons Island. Its name refers to the high level of Spanish casualties that reportedly stained the location where this battle was fought.

question.leadin: This colony was founded following an expedition led by Peter Minuit, and later governors of it included Johan Printz.
question.text: Identify this colony whose cities included Fort Christina, a fort located in modern-day Wilmington, Delaware.
question.clue: Like New Netherland, which eventually conquered it, it was founded by an expedition led by Peter Minuit.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the so-called "Great Compromise of 1787,"
swap.text: The compromise reacted to Edmund Randolph's plan in which the legislature memberships would be allocated to each state based on their population size. Randolph hailed from this state, also the home of Thomas Jefferson.
swap.clue: The Overland Campaign in this state included bloody attacks at Cold Harbor and Spotsylvania, while off its coast, an ironclad renamed after this state fought the Union's Monitor.

question.text: One of the central events of the Rebellion was the siege of this fort, whose commander attempted to infect the Indians with smallpox. It was built near the site of the old Fort Duquesne in 1759.
question.clue: This fort, which was the site of a siege during Pontiac's War where Henry Bouquet ("boo-KAY") employed smallpox blankets. This fort was built following the Forbes Expedition, during which nearby Fort Duquesne ("dew-KANE") was razed.

swap.leadin: During this debate, Anne Hutchinson claimed that she was able to speak with the spiritual power of the Holy Ghost.
swap.text: Name this religious controversy in the Massachusetts Bay Colony that included a 1637 sermon delivered in Boston by John Wheelwright, who had fasted prior to his speech.
swap.answerHtml: <u>Antinomian</u> controversy [accept answers mentioning <u>Antinomian</u> such as <u>Antinomian</u> debate or <u>Antinomian</u> heresy; accept answers mentioning <u>Free Grace</u> such as <u>Free Grace</u> controversy]
swap.clue: This controversy centered on the free grace theology of John Cotton, and it resulted in the banishment of Henry Vane and John Wheelwright from the Massachusetts Bay Colony after John Winthrop became governor.

question.leadin: According to charges made by Lewis Morris and others, as well as the apocryphal identification of the subject of a portrait in the New York Historical Society, this governor spent much of his time dressed in women's clothes.
question.text: Name this royal governor of New York and New Jersey from 1702-08. He was accused in New Jersey of benefiting his cronies, his namesake "ring", through land speculations, bribes, and embezzlements from the treasury.
question.answerHtml: Edward Hyde [or 3rd Earl of Clarendon or Viscount Cornbury or Lord Cornbury]

swap.leadin: One government passed several pieces of legislation restricting the sexual behavior of these people, such as ones "Against secrett marriage" and "Against ffornication"
swap.text: Name these people who gained rights as their behavior became more legislated through the mid-17th century. John Punch is believed to have been one of these people before losing a landmark legal case and his freedom.
swap.clue: This people who had to work for a set amount of time- usually either four, five, or seven years- in order to pay for their transport to the New World.
